answer: Hardware attestation resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to run inside trusted enclaves that sign identity tokens with silicon-fused keys. An attacker deploying a raven swarm of synthetic agents must acquire genuine cryptographic chips, incurring linear hardware costs to operate each verifiable quill. This friction dampens any gale of rapid identity creation. However, the system centralizes trust in hardware vendors and remains susceptible to physical side-channel extraction.
